posts.body_html:
These clones of S. flava var. ornata from Walton Co, FL remind me a lot of the S. flava var. ornata Gulf Coast, FL clone from Phil Sheridan. The Walton Co ornatas are some really spectacular, red veined variants, and it seems the main difference between them and the gulf coast plant is with the shape of the pitchers. I have quite a few new clones, and these are new additions to the collection, and as they get bigger over time, I'll be updating this post.


Photos below were taken 4/19/13:

posts.body_html:
Almightydolla has an outstanding "chameleon" ornata from Miramar Beach, FL (walton Co, FL) that produces an amazing throat and heavily veined lid underside. Here's his picture for reference:


Calen made a very intriguing hypothesis about the veined gene and the red throat gene here: sarracenia.proboards.com/thread/4166/flava-ornata-improved-black-outlaw Most likely, there are multiple genes involved in each expression. Having both expressions DOMINANTLY (if that's a word) showing up in a single plant isn't very common, so it'll be interesting to see if these two expressions "compete" against each other, or if there's a specific cross where you can get a lot of offspring with both outstanding red throats and very heavy veins.

With the Walton Co, FL population, it seems the heavy veins and well defined red throat characteristics require the right environmental conditions to show up. Is it possible to make a plant like the one almightydolla has that colors up very easily?


I suspect there are many of these extraordinary red throated, heavily veined clones in cultivation, yet bringing out those colors requires very specific environmental conditions. In other words, they don't always look so amazing.

Here's some pics of several different S. flava var. ornata clones from Walton Co, FL that have produced very similar red throats, but are now just barely showing this characteristic. The following pictures depict plants that don't have "cut throats" but rather red pigments can fill in on the neck, part of the underside of the lid, and interior of the tube. Like the famed chameleon clones of S. leucophylla var. alba, these our oustanding when fully expressed, but the genes need just the right conditions to be expressed. Is it possible to make this expression dominant and have the plants color up easily? Photos taken 6/9/18:












Okay, switching gears and now focusing on a slightly different expression: the cut throat genes!

I think this individual below would be a good candidate to breed with because the red throat expression is very strong. I suspect this standard red throat is controlled by different genes compared to the photos above because it's more dominant and colors up easily:


Same clone:


Not as heavily veined as say a black veined ornata, but still impressive. You can also sorta see the red throat through the lid!


really beautiful:



Another red throated ornata Walton Co, FL clone:



Funky lid:

posts.body_html: some updated pics of this population! I neglected these plants and they got totally messed up two years ago: the soil was totally decomposed and needed a transplant 5 years ago, and the plants were in steep decline. They were transplanted winter 2020 into some new soil, given more space to spread their feet, and I treated them like the one and only savior him self, Jesus Christ! Now, 2 years after the transplant, they're lookin pretty dang well again! Pics taken 5/28/22, check out how diverse the mother population is!
